newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec premier says sovereignty plans are intact.
newsitem.headline: Quebec premier says sovereignty plans are intact.

text.p: Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard said on Thursday the Canadian government's request for a Supreme Court ruling on Quebec separation will not affect his government's sovereignty referendum plans.
"It is certain that it will not affect in any way the future of Quebec and the determination of this government to hold a referendum," Bouchard told reporters in French at the provincial legislature.

Bouchard was reacting to the Canadian government's announcement on Wednesday that it would ask the country's Supreme Court to rule on the legality of any future unilateral declaration of independence by Quebec.
Asked whether the federal government's action would affect his "referendum calendar," Bouchard replied: "Not at all."
He said Quebec will continue to focus on putting its fiscal house in order and tackling its economic problems, including its high unemployement rate.

Bouchard has said previously that he would hold another referendum on Quebec sovereignty only after the next provincial election, which can be called at his government's discretion, but could be up to three years away.
Bouchard said Quebec will not appear before the Supreme Court to defend against the federal government's action on the sovereignty issue.
"This is not for a tribunal (court) to decide those questions," Bouchard said in English. Those questions are about the sovereignty of a will democratically expressed by a people."
